session: SNAP (human-assigned axis), response family: magnetic edges (tmi_hg / tc)

parent.evidence_class: CLAIM (owner-reported; no submission-page receipt in ledger/)

fixed_rule.window: 25 cells with max(|dy|,|dx|) <= 2 (brief: 'move each dot <= 2 px')
fixed_rule.spacing_floor_justification: identical to R0's own measured nearest-neighbour floor (the d2.8 rung), so SNAP can neither tighten nor loosen the emission spacing
destination_constraints: not within the spacing floor of another dot's source
not within the spacing floor of an already-placed dot
fixed_rule.determinism: no random draws; seed 0 recorded only to satisfy the reproducibility rule
fixed_rule.count: unchanged by construction (every dot ends at either a permitted destination or its own source)

why_smoothing_was_fixed_in_advance: A diagnostic run made before this file was written showed that snapping to the raw 100 m bands moves 99 % of dots with a per-dot gain barely above a random-offset null (mean gain 0.000 sigma against a null p90 of +0.288, 43 % of dots beating that null). That is interpolation jitter between the 400 m GeoDAWN flight lines, not an edge. Smoothing at one cell and gating on a 0.25 sigma gain are therefore part of the rule, not a result.

gate: file re-read from disk after writing
report_only: catalogue hide-and-recover PROXY with n withheld positives and 95% CI
leakage canary (single-feature catalogue AUC; > 0.90 stops the session)
H19-5 rank readout of the parent lineage
analysis_plan.evidence_floor: a live change under 0.01 is treated as no evidence
analysis_plan.no_label_probing: no region-isolated or patterned raster is built; nothing is submitted or scraped
